_about: PROPOSAL for 'PMG Build Instructions/trim.json' (read by trim_source.py): the parts the PMG Full Build shows, one copy each, where each sits when the game is built. Every other position the engineer modelled is a pose of these (docs/research/pmg/reuse_poses.json). Wire and cable bodies are left out: the player draws them from wire-paths.json, measured from the full pmg.glb first. Remove 'base' when this file sits in the kit folder.
_keep_about: NAUO78 the I/O module on H4; NAUO76 / 83 / 84 / 85 the buttons in the case (black, yellow, white, blue caps: D4 - D7); NAUO79 the 4-digit display on its brackets; NAUO81 the LED matrix in the case; NAUO60 - 75 and 77 the wood, H1 - H14 with four H9 keys (69 - 72); NAUO282 the right-angle Mini-B end plugged into the Nano on NAUO78; NAUO278 the USB A end (where it rests is the guide's choice); 34 jumper caps on the built parts' pins: 17 on NAUO78 (95 - 102, 111 - 119), 8 on the buttons (86 - 93), 4 on the display (259 - 262), 5 on the matrix (134 - 138).
_drop_about: NAUO301 is the plain Nano model (34 meshes, 213,141 vertices) that the I/O module's CAD carries inside it, the same as the RCC's car Nano NAUO86. The guide fits the MRA's Nano model instead (graft NANO below, or extra_parts).
_rename_about: the four caps are one mesh in the CAD (byte for byte): build_model.py shares identical geometry under one name, so without a name each, all four would take one colour. Colours from TechBox's PMG Cadasio project, matched by place.
_graft_about: the MRA's Nano Board (mra.glb NAUO126, the export the RCC also uses) carried by the transform that takes the MRA's I/O module onto NAUO78 (exact on all 36 of the module's meshes): it lands in the module's sockets, its board where the CAD's own plain Nano board is (to 0.01 mm). Named NANO: pmg.glb already has a part called NAUO126 (a jumper cap). Leave this out and use materials.json extra_parts instead if preferred (docs/research/pmg/reuse_plan.md 2.2).
